findings.problem: println! logging call fused inside load_frames parser alongside file I/O, CSV splitting, and domain construction
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic leaks side effects into the shell, making the function untestable in isolation and breaking Data/Calculations/Actions separation
findings.fix: Remove println! from load_frames; move all logging to a shell wrapper that calls a pure parse function

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, truncated read)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted filesystem input aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use ? to propagate the io::Error, or map to a domain LoadError variant

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data in any non-first field causes a panic instead of returning a typed parse error for that record
findings.fix: Replace with parts[1].trim().parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| LoadError::InvalidRecord) or use split_once with map_err for a typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] access vector indices derived from line.split(',').collect() with no bounds check, no get(), no split_once, and no minimum-length guard
findings.failure_mode: malformed lines with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields cause index-out-of-bounds panic; empty lines also panic
findings.fix: Replace split/collect/indexing with line.split_once(',').ok_or(LoadError::InvalidRecord)? and destructure into (_name, value_str); this avoids index access and bounds checking entirely

findings.problem: as u16 lossy cast from parsed u32 value silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 silently becomes 4448, corrupting domain data with no error indication to the caller
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| LoadError::ValueOutOfRange) to return a typed error when the value exceeds u16::MAX

findings.problem: load_frames fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), shell-side logging (println!), CSV parsing, domain construction, and unbounded Vec allocation into a single 15-line function
findings.failure_mode: no Data/Calculations/Actions separation; the parser cannot be unit-tested without a real file on disk, and side effects are indistinguishable from domain logic
findings.fix: Extract a pure parse_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> function, keep load_frames as the shell that reads the file, logs, calls parse_line per line, and collects into a Vec

findings.problem: load_frames allocates Vec<Record> from an unbounded file with no domain cap, no try_reserve, and no max_items guard on the outer collect
findings.failure_mode: a large or malicious input file causes unbounded heap allocation that can OOM the process with no graceful degradation
findings.fix: Accept a max_items parameter, create Vec::new(), call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after cap validation, enforce values.len() < max_items before each push, and return Err(LoadError::TooMany) when the cap is exceeded

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper, so file errors, parse errors, overflow errors, and allocation errors all collapse into panics
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish between I/O failure, malformed data, value overflow, or memory pressure; all failures are unrecoverable process aborts
findings.fix: Define a LoadError enum (Io, InvalidRecord, ValueOutOfRange, Allocation, TooMany), change the signature to Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, and propagate every fallible step with ?

findings.problem: raw String from CSV split crosses the parse boundary directly into Record without a fallible smart constructor; any caller can also construct Record{ name, value } directly with invalid data
findings.failure_mode: illegal states are representable: name can be empty, value can be any u16, and there is no validation at the boundary so the domain core cannot trust its inputs
findings.fix: Add a Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError> smart constructor that validates invariants, and make Record::new the only public path into the type

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames throughput or latency
no profiler data for allocation patterns in load_frames hot path
no second-ring evidence for zero-cost claims (none stated, but allocation discipline requires measured bounds)
no command evidence: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, or cargo check were not run
no max_items or domain cap documented for load_frames bounded allocation
residual_risk: Static review only. All 8 findings are BLOCKERs violating absolute laws of the Holzman candidate skill. The crate contains panic surfaces (2x unwrap), unchecked indexing, lossy cast, hidden I/O, unbounded allocation without try_reserve, no typed error taxonomy, no parse-boundary smart constructor, and fused shell/domain logic. No commands were executed. Delivery must be blocked until all blockers are repaired with typed errors, checked access, bounded allocation, and Data/Calculations/Actions separation.
